discovery: Discovery of high-temperature multiband superconductivity in magnesium diboride and iron-based compounds

nominees.name: Hideo Hosono
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Science Tokyo (formerly Tokyo Institute of Technology), Japan

motivation: In 2001 Akimitsu's group discovered superconductivity at 39 K in MgB2, a simple compound whose two distinct superconducting gaps made multiband pairing an experimental reality rather than a theoretical curiosity. In 2008 Hosono's group discovered superconductivity in LaFeAsO:F, opening the iron-based family, the second class of high-temperature superconductors, with critical temperatures above 50 K. These discoveries ended the belief that high-Tc superconductivity was confined to cuprates. They also established a new paradigm: superconductors with several coupled condensates, in which interband phase differences, sign-changing gaps, fractional vortices, broken time-reversal states and non-standard magnetic responses can occur. Both families now drive thousands of experimental and theoretical studies, and they have practical uses in wires and high-field magnets. Together these discoveries changed how physicists classify and understand superconducting states of matter.
